  "before": {
    "stem": "42. A mortgage by deposit of title-deeds is a form of mortgage recognised by section 58(f) of\nthe Transfer of Property Act, 1882, which provides that:",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "When the debtor deposits with the creditor the title-deeds of his property with an\nintent to create a security, the law implies a contract between the parties to create\na mortgage, and no registered instrument is required under section 59 of the\nTransfer of Property Act, as in other forms of mortgage."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "When the debtor deposits with the creditor the title-deeds of his property with an\nintent to create a security, the implication of law (that there exists a contract\nbetween the parties to create a mortgage) is excluded, and a registered instrument\nis required under section 59 of the Transfer of Property Act."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "When the debtor deposits with the creditor the title-deeds of his property with an\nintent to create a security, the implication of law (that there exists a contract\nbetween the parties to create a mortgage) is excluded, and a registered instrument\nis required under section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "When the debtor deposits with the creditor the title-deeds of his property with an\nintent to create a security, the implication of law (that there exists a contract\nbetween the parties to create a mortgage) is excluded, and a registered instrument\nis required under section 17(1)"
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(c)",
        "text": "of the Registration Act."
      }
    ]
  },

d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0020:l0000:question | primary_line_start_options_prior_cleaning_preserved
{
  "question_id": "d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0020:l0000:question",
  "rule": "primary_line_start_options_prior_cleaning_preserved",
  "before": {
    "stem": "45. In a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds, after the deposit of the title-deeds, if the creditor\nand the borrower choose to record their transaction in a memorandum reducing other\nterms and conditions (in addition to what flow from the mortgage by deposit of title-\ndeeds) with regard to the deposit in the form of a memorandum/document, then the\nmemorandum/document requires registration under section 17(1)",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(c)",
        "text": "of the Registration\nAct. In this context which among the following propositions is not correct?"
      },
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "The deposit and the document both form integral parts of the transaction and are\nessential ingredients in the creation of the mortgage."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "The deposit alone is not intended to create the charge and the document, which\nconstitutes the bargain regarding the security, is also necessary and operates to\ncreate the charge in conjunction with the deposit."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "The implication of law (that there exists a contract between the parties to create a\nmortgage) is excluded by their express bargain, and the document becomes the sole\nevidence of its terms."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "The deposit and the documents do not form integral parts of the transaction and\nhence they are not essential ingredients in the creation of the mortgage."
      }
    ]
  },
  "after": {
    "stem": "45. In a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds, after the deposit of the title-deeds, if the creditor and the borrower choose to record their transaction in a memorandum reducing other terms and conditions (in addition to what flow from the mortgage by deposit of title- deeds) with regard to the deposit in the form of a memorandum/document, then the memorandum/document requires registration under section 17(1)(c) of the Registration Act. In this context which among the following propositions is not correct?",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "The deposit and the document both form integral parts of the transaction and are essential ingredients in the creation of the mortgage."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "The deposit alone is not intended to create the charge and the document, which constitutes the bargain regarding the security, is also necessary and operates to create the charge in conjunction with the deposit."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "The implication of law (that there exists a contract between the parties to create a mortgage) is excluded by their express bargain, and the document becomes the sole evidence of its terms."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "The deposit and the documents do not form integral parts of the transaction and hence they are not essential ingredients in the creation of the mortgage."
      }
    ]
  },

d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0112:l0032:question | primary_line_start_options_prior_cleaning_preserved
{
  "question_id": "d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0112:l0032:question",
  "rule": "primary_line_start_options_prior_cleaning_preserved",
  "before": {
    "stem": "42. Srinivasan, J. in Mayawati v. Markandeya Chand held that ‘Political Party’ cannot be read\nas ‘legislature Party’. Which among the following was not a reason provided by the Hon’ble\nJudge?",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(a)",
        "text": "the phrase ‘Political Party’ in Paragraph 2(1)"
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(b)",
        "text": "of the tenth schedule cannot be\ninterpreted to mean ‘legislative Party’ while the same phrase in Paragraph 2(1)"
      },
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(a)",
        "text": "of\nthe tenth Schedule retains its original meaning."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "Such an interpretation would render explanation"
      },
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(a)",
        "text": "to Paragraph 2(1) of the tenth\nSchedule otiose because a legislature party cannot set up a person as a candidate for\nelection;"
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "Disqualification from membership of the assembly is a serious consequence. Such\na consequence can only ensue from voting contrary to the direction of the political\nparty."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(d)",
        "text": "in Kuldip nayar v. Union of india, it was held that to balance the competing considerations\nof the anti-defection law and intra-party dissent, a direction to vote (or abstain from\nvoting) can only be given if the vote would alter the status of the government formed\nor if it is on a policy on which the political party that set up the candidate went to polls\non. only the political party and not the legislature party can issue directions concerning\nissues of this nature."
      }
    ]

  "before": {
    "passage_id": null,
    "stem": "9. Consider the given statements.\n(I) For seeking the intervention of the court, the petitioner has to prima facie establish that\nthe State agency has misused the force of criminal law which causes casualty for the\nhuman liberty.\n(II) The deprivation of liberty via rule by law is bearable up to twenty-four hours.\nChoose the correct answer from the code given below."
  },
  "after": {
    "passage_id": "d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0229:l0019:passage",
    "stem": "9. Consider the given statements. (I) For seeking the intervention of the court, the petitioner has to prima facie establish that the State agency has misused the force of criminal law which causes casualty for the human liberty. (II) The deprivation of liberty via rule by law is bearable up to twenty-four hours. Choose the correct answer from the code given below."
  },
  "source_evidence": [

{
  "question_id": "d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0231:l0015:question",
  "rule": "explicit_answer_delimited_question_and_passage",
  "before": {
    "passage_id": null,
    "stem": "14. Based on the given excerpt from a judgment, which of the following was not a direction\ngiven by the Supreme Court of India?",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "Women officers on Short Service Commission with more than twelve years of\nservice who do not opt for being considered for the grant of the Permanent\nCommissions will be entitled to continue in service until they complete twenty-two\nyears of pensionable service."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "Short Service Commission women officers with over twenty years of service who\nare not granted Permanent Commission shall retire on pension in terms of the policy\ndecision."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "All serving women officers on Short Service Commission shall be considered for\nthe grant of Permanent Commission irrespective of any of them having completed\nfourteen years or, as the case may be, twenty years of service."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "Short Service Commission women officers who are granted Permanent Commission\nin pursuance of the above directions will be entitled to all consequential benefits\nincluding promotion and financial benefits."
      }
    ]
  },

        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "Equality should not ensure that where the action of the State does differentiate\nbetween two classes of persons, it does not differentiate them in an unreasonable or\nirrational manner."
      },

        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "An absolute bar on women seeking criteria or command appointments would not\ncomport with the guarantee of equality under Article 14 of the Constitution of India."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "Where the Army as an instrumentality of the State, differentiates between women\nand men, the burden does not fall on the Army to justify such differentiation with\nreason."

    "stem": "35. As per the given excerpt from a judgment, which of the following is correct in relation to\nthe living status of a father in ensuring coparcenary property rights to a daughter?",

      {
        "label": "A",

    "stem": "66. When a court summons any person as a witness upon allowing an application made by the\naccused under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, which of the\nfollowing statements is correct?",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "An opportunity of rebuttal must not be given to the prosecution."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "An opportunity of rebuttal must be given to the prosecution."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "There is no question of rebuttal as the witness has been summoned by the court."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "Whether opportunity of rebuttal is given to the prosecution or not is matter of\ndiscretion of the court."
      }
    ]
  },

    "stem": "70.   },
  "after": {

d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0246:l0036:question | explicit_answer_delimited_question_and_passage
{
  "question_id": "d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0246:l0036:question",
  "rule": "explicit_answer_delimited_question_and_passage",
  "before": {
    "passage_id": null,
    "stem": "74. According to the provisions of the Extradition Act, 1962, where there is no extradition\ntreaty made by India with a foreign State, which of the following is correct?",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "The Central Government may, by notified order, treat any Convention to which India\nand the foreign State are parties, as an extradition treaty made by India with that\nforeign State."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "The Central Government may, by law, treat any Convention to which India is a party,\nas an extradition treaty made by India with that foreign State."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "The Central Government may, by notified order, treat the pari materia provisions of\nthe statutes of both States relating to extradition, as an extradition treaty made by\nIndia with that foreign State."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "Extradition is not permissible."

    "stem": "74. According to the provisions of the Extradition Act, 1962, where there is no extradition treaty made by India with a foreign State, which of the following is correct?",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "The Central Government may, by notified order, treat any Convention to which India and the foreign State are parties, as an extradition treaty made by India with that foreign State."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "The Central Government may, by law, treat any Convention to which India is a party, as an extradition treaty made by India with that foreign State."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "The Central Government may, by notified order, treat the pari materia provisions of the statutes of both States relating to extradition, as an extradition treaty made by India with that foreign State."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "Extradition is not permissible."
      }
    ]
  },

        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "(A)",
        "text": "It contemplates legal proceedings for vindication or enforcement of fundamental\nrights of a group of persons or community which are not able to enforce their\nfundamental rights on account of their incapacity, poverty or ignorance of law."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",
        "text": "A person invoking the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 must\napproach the court for the vindication of the fundamental rights of affected persons."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "(C)",
        "text": "Recourse to a proceeding under Article 32 may or may not be taken by a genuinely\ninterested person in protection of society on behalf of community."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "(D)",
        "text": "Personal interest, grudge or enmity cannot be enforced through the process of the\ncourt, preventing speedy remedy to the other genuine petitioners from the court."

  "before": {
    "passage_id": null,
    "stem": "95. “If a citizen is no more than a wayfarer or officious intervener without any interest or\nconcern beyond what belongs to any one of the 660 million people of this country, the\ndoor of the court will not be ajar for him.         "label": "A",

      },

        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "(B)",

{
  "question_id": "d3905f6d3c31af4cdf5d47d3e6380179c5fd2c8f55e489648d140783b06a0d3b:p0259:l0010:question",
  "rule": "explicit_answer_delimited_question_and_passage",
  "before": {
    "passage_id": null,
    "stem": "3. The Union government has issued an office memorandum under which 3% reservation\nhas been provided to the persons with disability, apart from the reservations provided to\ndifferent class of citizens such as 27% for OBCs, 14% to SCs and & 7% to STs. Now, the\ntotal percentage of reservation has reached 51%, which is against the judgment given in\nIndira Sawhney v. Union of India. Now, choose the most appropriate option amongst the\nfollowing.",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "a)",
        "text": "The reservation provided to persons with disability is constitutionally valid as it falls\nwithin the horizontal scheme of reservation."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "b)",
        "text": "The judgment in Indira Sawhney is not applicable to the persons with disability and hence\nsuch reservation is valid."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "c)",
        "text": "The reservation provided to persons with disability is invalid as in no case reservation can\nincrease 50%."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "d)",
        "text": "The reservation to PWD does not fall under the scheme of Article 16 (4) and hence\nunconstitutional."
      }
    ]
  },

    "stem": "50. Suppose, students filled up JEE Mains form for 2020. Due to repeated postponements of\nJEE, IIT Kharagpur decided to opt out of JEE mains and conducted its own separate Test.\nOn which of the following grounds the decision of IIT Kharagpur can be challenged?",
    "options": [
      {
        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "a)",
        "text": "Procedural fairness"
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "b)",
        "text": "Legitimate expectation"
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "c)",
        "text": "Manifest arbitrariness"
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "d)",
        "text": "IIT Kharagpur‘s decision cannot be challenged as it was taken in the interest of the\nstudents."
      }
    ]
  },

    "stem": "84. Which one of the following statements, correctly conveys the Fuller‘s Inner Morality of\nLaw?",
    "options": [

        "label": "A",
        "raw_label": "a)",
        "text": "Every piece of Law, in order to be valid, must fulfil minimum moral standard comprising\nof certain procedural requirements like generality, Prospectively promulgation, intelligibility\nand consistency."
      },
      {
        "label": "B",
        "raw_label": "b)",
        "text": "The contents of every law in order to be valid must be mere minimum moral standard\nwithout anything more."
      },
      {
        "label": "C",
        "raw_label": "c)",
        "text": "The question of morality of every law is a matter for the inner conscience of the legislators\nand judges have nothing to do with it."
      },
      {
        "label": "D",
        "raw_label": "d)",
        "text": "The question of morality of law is not for the courts to determine."
      }

    "stem": "104. Which one of the following is not correctly matched? 1. Talak Ahsan--This consists of three pronouncement of divorces made during a tuhr (period between menstruations) followed by abstinence from sexual intercourse for the period of iddat. 2. Talak Hasan- This consists of three pronouncements made during successive tuhrs, no intercourse taking place during any of the three tuhrs. The first pronouncement should be made during a tuhr, the second during the next tuhr, and the third during the succeeding tuhr. 3. Talak-ul-Bidaat - This consists of – (i) Three pronouncements made during a single tuhr either in one sentence, e.g., ―I divorce thee thrice,‖ - or in separate sentences e.g., ―I divorce thee, I divorce thee, I divorce thee‖, 4. Talak-ul-Bidaat - This consists of – (ii) a single pronouncement made during a tuhr clearly indicating an intention irrevocably to dissolve the marriage, e.g., “I divorce thee irrevocably.”"
  },
